calls.body: The Maple Leafs’ power play is near the top of the league, and the Kraken’s kill is one of the worst. Every trip to the box hurts the Kraken more than most.

calls.head: The Kraken roll four lines, the Maple Leafs lean on their top six
calls.body: On depth, Seattle is one of the league’s best, but Toronto is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Kraken.

surprises.head: Toronto couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Toronto usually gets worse looks than most teams, and Seattle usually allows fewer dangerous shots than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a night of harmless shots: Toronto’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 2.9% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.0% (about 5.7% against Seattle) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 150 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Montour scores with 33 seconds left to lift the Kraken
paras: Berkly Catton got the scoring started for the Kraken just under two minutes in, but Gavin McKenna tied it 1-1 for Toronto on the power play late in the first. The second period was a wild one. Josh Mahura put the Kraken back ahead 2-1 just 16 seconds into the period. McKenna struck again on the power play a minute and a half later to tie it 2-2. Chandler Stephenson restored the Kraken’s lead on the power play less than two minutes later, and Ryker Evans made it 4-2 midway through the second. Cale Fleury and Vinni Lettieri dropped the gloves later in the period. The Kraken went more than 17 minutes of the third period without a shot on goal. Jack Roslovic pulled the Maple Leafs within one midway through the third. With the goalie pulled and a minute and a half left, Auston Matthews tied it 4-4, and Brandon Montour put the Kraken ahead for good with 33 seconds left. Two players had three-point nights: Matthews with a goal and two assists, and McKenna with two goals and an assist.

The Kraken had a bit more of the good stuff. Philipp Grubauer made 17 saves for the Kraken, and Sergei Bobrovsky allowed five goals on 17 shots. The Kraken improved to 8-4-1, third in the Pacific, while the Maple Leafs dropped to 7-6-2, fifth in the Atlantic.
